newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury sets out banking stall.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury sets out banking stall.

text.p: British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc launched its joint venture Sainsbury's Bank on Wednesday, offering high interest and loyalty points in the latest tussle for market share in the sector.

Initial offers from Sainsbury's Bank, in which the grocery chain holds 55 percent and Bank of Scotland has 45 percent, include an Instant Access account offering 5.75 percent annual interest and Visa credit cards, in three different colour choices.
Customers will also gain extra points under Sainsbury's Reward loyalty scheme for using certain services.
"They are not unattractive offers and they should appeal to customers," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"Our customers trust us to deliver service and value for money," marketing director Kevin McCarten said.
Sainsbury is hoping that the bank will enhance customer loyalty and give an added marketing thrust to its brand, company spokesman Dominic Fry said.
Sainsbury is the first of the big four supermarkets to branch into banking, although market leader Tesco has linked up with Royal Bank of Scotland and Safeway with Abbey National .
